title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing and padding minimization heuristics (v14)
author: Aisha Kumar
description:
Motivation: the continuous batching layer currently pads requests to the max sequence length in the batch which wastes GPU cycles for skewed seqlen distributions. This PR implements a seqlen bucketing + padding-minimization heuristic that groups requests by percentile-based buckets at queueing time, computes an adaptive padding target per bucket, and surfaces lightweight telemetry so we can tune defaults per workload.

What this PR does: implements a two-stage heuristic in the runtime dispatcher: 1) an inexpensive seqlen bucketer that groups in-flight requests into a small number of buckets derived from recent seqlen percentiles (p10/p50/p90/p99), and 2) a padding target selector that chooses the minimal padding point for the bucket subject to a latency SLO budget and a small headroom factor to avoid frequent re-batching. The dispatcher supports soft-fallbacks: if a bucket cannot be filled within a short timeout we fall back to the existing batching strategy to preserve latency SLOs.

Key design notes: - Bucket counts are limited to 3 by default (low/medium/high) to keep scheduling overhead low and avoid fragmentation. - The percentile estimators are exponentially-weighted histograms with a bounded memory footprint and cheap updates on enqueue. - The padding model tracks wasted-token cost vs throughput using online counters; this data feeds the Optimize recommendations service. - We added a conservative safety toggle (env var + runtime config) so Dedicated tenants can opt-in gradually.

Compatibility and correctness: changes are backward-compatible at the API layer. The heuristic is purely scheduling-level and does not alter model kernels or KV cache semantics. We ensure KV cache hits are preserved by maintaining request ordering and per-request kv-id mapping when re-batching occurs.

Testing and validation: microbenchmarks show 9-16% throughput improvement on multi-tenant mixed seqlen workloads and 12-18% reduction in padding tokens for typical chat workloads. End-to-end SLO e2e tests were added and CI includes a perf-canary job that runs against a small GPU cluster simulation.

Rollout plan: feature-gated behind runtime flag (runtime.features.seqlen_bucketing) and off by default for Hosted; enabled for internal perf experiments. We'll rollout to Dedicated perf ring then enable for a small % of Hosted traffic while monitoring wasted_token and latency P99 metrics.

References: ENG-1482 (design doc), SUP-4021 (customer incident that motivated quick improvement).
